programme.title: Life of a Mountain: A Year on Blencathra
programme.desc: Terry Abraham returns to the Lake District to showcase `the people's mountain', Blencathra. It looks at the lives of local residents, school children and visitors to the mountain with contributions from celebrities.

programme.title: Woolly Mammoth: Secrets from the Ice
programme.desc: Professor Alice Roberts reveals the natural history of the Ice Age's woolly mammoth. Mammoths have transfixed humans since the depths of the last Ice Age when their herds roamed across what is now Europe and Asia. Although extinct for thousands of years, scientists can now paint an incredibly detailed picture of their lives thanks to whole carcasses beautifully preserved in the Siberian permafrost.

programme.title: The Truth About Christmas Carols
programme.desc: There could be nothing more sweet and sentimental than the sound of traditional carols performed by a velvet-voiced choir at Christmas, or so you would think. Composer Howard Goodall uncovers the surprising and often secret history of the Christmas carol. Far from being accepted as part of the celebrations of Jesus' birth, over the centuries carols have been banned by both church and state.

programme.title: Winter Walks

programme.title: Winter's Weirdest Events
programme.desc: Chris Packham examines the evidence, tests the theories and unravels some of the strangest stories the planet has to offer. Based in a remote hut for the winter, Chris embarks on a journey to try to explain some of winter's weirdest events.

programme.title: Leonardo
programme.sub-title: The Secret Life of the Mona Lisa
programme.desc: Alan Yentob tells the story of the creation of the world's most famous work of art. She has her own bodyguards and lives in Paris in a humidified, air-conditioned box protected by triplex bullet proof glass. Despite this she is visited by six million tourists every year. She is Leonardo da Vinci's Mona Lisa.

programme.title: Britain's Pompeii: A Village Lost in Time
programme.desc: Professor Alice Roberts joins the team excavating a 3,000 year-old Bronze Age village in the Cambridgeshire Fens that's been called the `British Pompeii'. The village earned its nickname because, 3,000 years ago, it burned to the ground - as it burned, it fell into the peat, preserving both the houses and their contents. Until its discovery, we had little real idea of what life was like in Bronze Age Britain.

programme.title: On Camera: Photographers at the BBC
programme.desc: Drawing on the BBC's rich archive, this programme reveals the working practices, lives and opinions of some of the greatest photographers of the last 60 years.

programme.title: The Magical World of Julia Donaldson
programme.desc: A celebration of the life and work of one of Britain's best-selling children's authors, with unique access to Julia Donaldson, her family, her rich archives and home movies, and the remarkable cast of characters that have sprung from her imagination. Specially commissioned animated illustrations from her long-term illustrator Axel Scheffler will bring Julia's biography to life.

programme.title: Turtle, Eagle, Cheetah: A Slow Odyssey
programme.desc: Join three young cheetah siblings, orphans, as they set out across the savannah in Namibia in search of prey. The orphaned cats are being reintroduced into the wilds of Namibia and specially designed on-board cameras are being used to monitor their progress. The summer rains have turned the land into a verdant scene, unleashing new sounds, sights and smells for the young cats to experience.
